criteria.text: Before changing any data, the response presents a summary table with the columns Column, Issue, Count, and Proposed Fix. The table lists the detected issues per column.

Where a formula equivalent exists (e.g., TRIM, VALUE/SUBSTITUTE, UPPER/PROPER, DATEVALUE), the response writes cleaning formulas into adjacent helper columns. It does not overwrite the originals with hardcoded computed values, unless the user explicitly asked for in-place changes.
criteria.source: Step 4: Prefer formulas over hardcoded cleaned values

criteria.text: Before any destructive operation (removing duplicates, filling blanks, or overwriting original values), the response asks the user for confirmation. It does not perform the operation without that confirmation.

The response profiles each column's dominant type (text/number/date) and checks the relevant issue categories from the detection list: whitespace, casing, number-as-text, mixed date formats, duplicates (including near-duplicates), blanks, mixed types, encoding/mojibake, and error values like #REF!/#N/A.
criteria.source: Step 1 profiling and Step 2: Detect issues table

criteria.text: The response applies fixes one category at a time, in the order whitespace → casing → number conversion → dates → dedup. After each category it shows a sample of the changes and asks for confirmation before moving on.
criteria.source: Step 4: After each category of fix...

criteria.text: The response matches the tooling to the environment. Inside Excel it uses Office JS (Excel.run, range.values, range.formulas). For a standalone .xlsx file it uses Python/openpyxl.
The response scopes its work correctly. It uses the user-specified range if one was given, and otherwise the full used range of the active sheet.
After applying fixes, the response gives a before/after summary of what changed, such as counts per issue type and the cells or columns affected.

The response overwrites values in place with computed results only when no sensible formula equivalent exists (e.g., mojibake/encoding repair) or when the user explicitly asks for it. It notes when it does so.
